runs.text: On Tuesday evening, the Millbrook Hollow City Council passed a modified version of the parks and recreation budget item. The same meeting also included some discussion of the long-stalled Third Street bridge replacement. A representative from the mayor's office said the updated figure came out of "ongoing conversations" between council members, but wouldn't offer any more detail about what those conversations involved. Two council staffers pointed to a separate memo from the finance subcommittee that put the change at roughly $340,000 — an amount a budget analyst who looked over the memo described as "in the range we expected." Toward the end of that same memo was a detail that no council member brought up during the meeting: the bridge's lead structural engineer had identified a load-bearing crack serious enough that the span would need to be closed to truck traffic within 90 days. The bridge project itself — on the capital plan since at least 2019 and already the subject of 14 change orders — wasn't discussed at any length. Afterward, council member Dana Okafor told reporters simply that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
